title: Keep Telegram prompt-target selectors in parity
outcome: Add a shared predicate or parity coverage if latest_project_prompt_target_session and find_latest_telegram_project_prompt_session diverge beyond their SessionRecord vs /api/state projection split.
acceptance:
C1 (a shared parity matrix with an oracle).
- A new test module, src/tests/prompt_target_parity.rs, holds one table of cases.
- Each case lists sessions once (id, project, parent delegation, status) and its expected target id, or none.
- Each case is projected into the digest's input (that project's sessions only, in order) and into Telegram's /api/state input (all projects' sessions, in order).
- For every case, the test asserts that both selectors return the SAME id, or both none, AND that this equals the case's expected oracle.

C3 (the real projection differences are kept, not papered over).
- A separate test states each difference with its own oracle:
  - Telegram's `Unknown` status, its serde fallback with no digest counterpart, is a prompt target;
  - Telegram filters by project_id itself, while the digest receives an already project-scoped list.
- The module header names these differences.

C4 (test-only, a mechanical carry).
- The change is the new module plus ONE registration line at the end of the mod list in src/tests/mod.rs.
- src/api.rs and src/telegram_digest.rs are unchanged, as is all production code.
- Every existing test still passes.

C5 (validation and landing).
- The full gate passes on the exact tree submitted for landing.
- The review pair has no outstanding finding of Medium or higher on it.
- The item carries the evidence the standing landing rule requires.
